    1. handle(HttpRequest, PathVariables, SseEmitter)

Interface SseHandler

Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface SseHandler
The handler of a server-sent events route: it pushes events to the client through an SseEmitter. See SseEmitter for when the response is sent, and for backpressure.

The stream ends when the handler returns: it is completed, or failed with the exception the handler threw, which is answered by the error routes if no event was sent yet. A handler that sends its events later, from callbacks or another thread, calls SseEmitter.keepOpen() and ends the stream itself, or lets it end when the client disconnects.

The handler runs like the handler of an asynchronous route: on the event loop unless the route executes on an executor. On an executor it may block, and pace itself with SseEmitter.sendAndAwait(Event): the response is sent while it still runs. A HEAD request runs the handler too, and sends the headers of the stream without its events.

// event driven: keep the stream open, and let it end with the connection
routes.GET("/prices").sse((request, pathVariables, events) -> {
    Subscription subscription = prices.subscribe(price -> {
        if (events.isWritable()) {
            events.send(Event.of(price).name("price"));
        }
    });
    events.keepOpen().heartbeat(Duration.ofSeconds(15)).onClose(error -> subscription.cancel());
});

// blocking, on virtual threads: the stream ends when the handler returns
routes.GET("/jobs/{id}/log").executeOn(TaskExecutors.VIRTUAL).sse((request, pathVariables, events) -> {
    for (LogLine line : jobs.tail(pathVariables.getString("id"), events.lastEventId())) {
        events.sendAndAwait(Event.of(line.text()).id(line.offset()));
    }
});

      void handle(HttpRequest<?> request, PathVariables pathVariables, SseEmitter events) throws Exception
      Run the stream.
      Parameters:
      request - The request
      pathVariables - The path variables of the matched route
      events - The emitter of the events of the response
      Throws:
      Exception - An error: before the first event, it is answered by the error routes like the error of any route, after it, the stream ends abruptly
